CreateMeetingSessionRequest.description:
Request body for creating a new meeting session.

Cross-field rules:
- `assistant` cannot be combined with `join_at`; it is available only for sessions that join immediately.
- `assistant` cannot be combined with `barge_in: true`.
- `assistant.avatar: true` cannot be combined with `speak_on_enter`; the assistant greets through its avatar.
- The `assistant` options, including `avatar`, take effect at session creation and cannot be modified later.
- An avatar takes precedence over `camera_image`; ordinary assistant sessions can use a static camera image.

Google Meet and Teams recording requires a recording_export destination. Use join_at to schedule a meeting, or omit it to join now. Zoom recordings are enabled automatically; Zoom does not support recording, recording_view or recording_export, and ignores leave_policy. Digital avatars require avatar support.

barge_in.description: When enabled, a human participant `speech_on` event interrupts and stops the current bot audio; it does not bypass admission or initiate speech. Assistant sessions reject `barge_in: true`.

bot_name.description: Display name for the bot in the meeting. Defaults to "Meeting Bot".

chat_on_enter.description: A message the bot posts to the meeting's chat as soon as it becomes active — typically a recording disclosure. Delivered at most once. Independent of `speak_on_enter`: both may be set, and the chat message posts first because it does not wait for text-to-speech or avatar startup. Rejected with 422 `unsupported_capability` on platforms without meeting chat. For Google Meet and Teams, text must be nonblank, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes, with no control characters except tabs and line breaks. Counts toward the 1000-chat-request session limit.

idempotency_key.description: Use a unique key per intended join and reuse the same key and request on retries. Reusing a key with a different join configuration or meeting URL can return 409 invalid_state. Always retry with the original request.

join_at.description: Future ISO-8601 join timestamp including timezone. Google Meet and Teams accept dates at most three years ahead. Omit for an immediate join. Assistant sessions created through this endpoint must join immediately.

meeting_url.description: The meeting URL the bot should join.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to the session. The serialized JSON representation must not exceed 16384 characters at runtime.

recording.description: Google Meet and Teams only. Defaults to true when recording_export is supplied and false otherwise. True requires recording_export.bucket; false cannot be combined with recording_export. Fixed at creation, with no pause/resume action. Zoom rejects recording, recording_view, and recording_export with 422 unsupported_capability; omit these fields for Zoom.

recording_view.description: Recording layout for Google Meet and Teams. Defaults to speaker_view. Accepted at creation only; does not enable recording by itself.

speak_on_enter.description: Text the bot speaks after joining. Available for sessions without a digital avatar. With an AI Assistant, the greeting waits until the assistant is connected. Rejected with 400 invalid_request when assistant.avatar is true.

summarize_on_end.description: If true, generate a summary artifact when the session ends.

voice.description: Session-default voice identifier used for `speak_on_enter` and ordinary speak actions. A voice supplied on an individual speak action overrides this default for that utterance. With an assistant attached, its conversational voice remains configured on the assistant.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS endpoint to receive session lifecycle callbacks. Static validation requires HTTPS, rejects embedded credentials and blocked hosts, and enforces egress policy. Validation makes no network request to the endpoint.

MeetingSession.description: Represents a meeting session. Core serializer fields are required; platform-specific fields are optional. Nullable fields use null when absent. No actor, provider-bot, idempotency, routing, key, or internal fields are exposed.

assistant.description: Assistant configuration if an assistant is attached, otherwise null.

assistant_state.description: Current state of the assistant, or null if no assistant is attached.

assistant_state_changed_at.description: Timestamp of the last assistant state change, or null.

avatar.description: The assistant's avatar when the session was created with `assistant.avatar: true`, otherwise null.

avatar_state.description: Current state of the avatar, or null if the session has no avatar. `starting` until the avatar's video is playing, then `connected`; `degraded` when the session has fallen back to voice-only (the `avatar.degraded` event carries the reason); `disconnected` when the avatar has ended.

avatar_state_changed_at.description: Timestamp of the last avatar state change, or null.

bot_name.description: Display name of the bot in the meeting.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

ended_at.description: Timestamp when the session ended, or null if ongoing.

failure_reason.description: A machine-readable lifecycle reason, or null. Values include left_on_request, meeting_ended, everyone_left, no_one_joined, silence_timeout, max_duration_reached, admission_timeout, admission_denied, removed_from_meeting, recording_permission_denied, meeting_not_found, meeting_not_started, meeting_access_denied, meeting_full, cancelled, cancelled_calendar_disconnected, cancelled_calendar_event_deleted, cancelled_calendar_superseded, cancelled_policy, internal_error, and other. Treat this vocabulary as extensible.

id.description: Unique identifier for the meeting session.

join_at.description: Scheduled join time, or null for immediate join.

joined_at.description: Timestamp when the session first became `active`, or null if it never became active. This remains positive admission evidence after terminal transitions.

meeting_url.description: The meeting URL the bot joins.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to the session.

recording.description: Whether the session is being recorded.

recording_export.description: Included on Google Meet and Teams create/retrieve responses, omitted from lists and update/leave responses. Null when disabled or no export reference is available.

remote_state_observed_at.description: Optional observation time on session list items. Retrieve the individual session when current state is required.

status.description: Lifecycle status. `waiting_for_admission` means the bot reached the meeting lobby and may require host approval. `active` means the bot entered the meeting/media path. `ended` alone does not prove attendance; use non-null `joined_at` as positive evidence that the session became active. `admission_denied` is reserved for an explicit provider denial, while cancellation or another termination can end a never-admitted session as `ended`.

status_detail.description: A machine-readable lifecycle reason, or null. Values include left_on_request, meeting_ended, everyone_left, no_one_joined, silence_timeout, max_duration_reached, admission_timeout, admission_denied, removed_from_meeting, recording_permission_denied, meeting_not_found, meeting_not_started, meeting_access_denied, meeting_full, cancelled, cancelled_calendar_disconnected, cancelled_calendar_event_deleted, cancelled_calendar_superseded, cancelled_policy, internal_error, and other. Treat this vocabulary as extensible.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update to the session.

webhook_url.description: Webhook endpoint for session lifecycle callbacks, or null if not configured.

audio_gate.description: Audio gating strategy in force for the assistant call leg.

dynamic_variables.description: Dynamic variables in individual-session responses; null when none were supplied. Omitted from session list items.

leave_on_end.description: Whether the bot leaves when the Assistant's conversation ends or fails.

MeetingSessionAssistantRequest.description: Attach a Telnyx AI Assistant owned by the authenticated account. Supply its ID and optional conversation settings. Unknown fields are rejected.

audio_gate.description: Use half_duplex (default) to pause listening while the assistant speaks, or full_duplex to allow participants to interrupt. Full-duplex pricing depends on participant audio usage; see the Meeting pricing guide.

avatar.description: Beta. Show the avatar configured on the assistant (its `avatar_settings`; see [AI Assistant avatars](/docs/inference/ai-assistants/avatars)) as the bot's camera, lip-synced to the assistant's own speech. The request carries no avatar ID or key: the assistant is read at creation and the request is rejected with 400 `invalid_request` if it has no Telnyx avatar configured. Available for Google Meet, Zoom, and Teams sessions. REST-only. Not echoed back on `assistant`; the session's top-level `avatar` and `avatar_state` fields report it instead. If the avatar fails, the session continues voice-only and `avatar_state` becomes `degraded`.

dynamic_variables.description: Per-conversation values for the [dynamic variables](/docs/inference/ai-assistants/dynamic-variables) used in the Assistant's instructions, greeting, or tools. Delivered before the Assistant's first utterance, so they resolve for the opening line as well as the rest of the conversation. At most 63 entries; keys 1-128 characters; values must be strings. The map is budgeted in aggregate at 1,047,552 bytes (1023 KiB) rather than capped per value. `streaming_audio`, `ai_assistant_streaming_audio` and `meeting_session_id` are reserved and rejected with `400 invalid_request`.

id.description: Identifier of the assistant to attach.

leave_on_end.description: Leave when the assistant conversation ends or fails. Defaults to false. Other leave-policy rules and explicit leave requests still apply.

MeetingSessionAvatar.description: The assistant's avatar, captured from its `avatar_settings` when the session was created. For display only; later changes to the assistant do not update it.

MeetingSessionCameraImage.description: Not supported for Google Meet and Teams joins (422 unsupported_capability). Write-only static camera-tile image for this session, not an account or participant profile photo. Supply exactly one JPEG source. When effective, the image is used as the bot's static camera/video output; presentation varies by meeting platform and recording configuration and is not guaranteed in recordings. An attached assistant or avatar takes precedence, so this input is ignored and a URL source is not fetched.
MeetingSessionCameraImage.title: MeetingSessionCameraImage

base64_data.description: Canonical plain RFC 4648 Base64 for a valid decoded JPEG. Data URIs, whitespace, and the URL-safe alphabet are rejected. The encoded value is limited to 1,835,008 characters and the decoded JPEG to 1,363,148 bytes. The JPEG is limited to 4,096 pixels per dimension, 4 megapixels, and 128 MB of decoder memory. The image bytes are not returned in the session response.

url.description: Public HTTPS JPEG URL with at most 2,048 characters and no credentials, fragment, surrounding whitespace, raw control characters, or explicit non-default port. Signed queries are allowed but must be treated as credentials. Fetching is limited to public network destinations, a five-second timeout, no redirects, a 2xx image/jpeg response with identity or no content encoding, and a 1,363,148-byte limit enforced against both declared and streamed content. The service resolves the URL before bot creation and does not return the URL or image bytes in the session response.

barge_in.description: When enabled, a human participant `speech_on` event interrupts and stops the current bot audio; it does not bypass admission or initiate speech. Assistant sessions reject `barge_in: true`.

chat_on_enter.description: The message posted to chat on join, or null when unset.

get.description: Returns a list of meeting sessions, optionally filtered by status. List items omit assistant.dynamic_variables and recording_export. Some items include remote_state_observed_at; retrieve the individual session for current state.

parameters.description: Filter meeting sessions by current status.
parameters.name: status

schema.description: Lifecycle status of the session. `scheduled`: waiting for `join_at` before the bot attempts to join. `joining`: the bot is connecting to the meeting. `waiting_for_admission`: the bot is in the lobby waiting to be admitted. `active`: the bot is in the meeting and capturing. `leaving`: the bot is exiting the meeting. `ended`: the bot left and the session is complete. `failed`: the bot could not join or the session failed. `admission_denied`: the host did not admit the bot.

200.description: Successful response with a list of meeting sessions.

post.description: Creates a meeting session and returns 201, or 200 for a replay. Use a unique `idempotency_key` per intended join and reuse the same key and request on retries. Reusing a key with a different join configuration or meeting URL can return 409 invalid_state. Always retry with the original request. The session can pass through joining and waiting_for_admission before active. Optional `camera_image` input is write-only and applies when no assistant avatar takes precedence. An ignored URL is not fetched. An effective URL source is resolved before bot creation; the source URL and image bytes are not returned in the session response. Treat signed URLs as credentials. With `assistant.avatar: true`, the assistant is read before the bot is created: an assistant without a Telnyx avatar configured is rejected with 400 `invalid_request` (message prefix `assistant_avatar_not_configured:`), an unknown assistant with 400 `invalid_request` (prefix `assistant_not_found:`), and a failed lookup with 503 `assistant_lookup_unavailable`; no bot is created in any of these cases.

200.description: Replayed existing meeting session matching the account-scoped idempotency_key. Replay is key-only; the request payload is not fingerprinted or compared.

error.message: The idempotency key belongs to a different join

409.description: The idempotency key belongs to a different or cancelled join.

delete.description: Stops a meeting session without deleting its persisted record. Scheduled bots are cancelled, while bots that are joining or active are asked to leave. The persisted meeting session record remains available. A successful response can report leaving while departure is pending. Poll until ended, failed, or admission_denied. Exported Storage objects are unaffected.

200.description: Successful response with the deleted meeting session.

get.description: Retrieves a single meeting session by ID. A session that does not exist or that belongs to a different account both return 404.

200.description: Successful response with the meeting session.

patch.description: Updates mutable properties of a meeting session. Only sessions in the scheduled state can be updated; any other state returns 409 with the invalid_state error code. All request fields are optional, and an empty object is a valid no-op update. Calendar-controlled Google Meet and Teams sessions return 409 calendar_managed; change the event instead. A conflicting pending edit returns 409 edit_in_progress. On a timeout or 503, read the session and retry the same changes.

200.description: Successful response with the updated meeting session.
